newsitem.title: USA: Enron sets sights on electric market share.
newsitem.headline: Enron sets sights on electric market share.

text.p: Enron Corp has set its sights on capturing a 10-percent share of the $215 billion a year North American electricity retail market by 2001, company executives said on Wednesday.

The company, which used this year's Super Bowl to kick off a nationwide image-advertising campaign, expects to rack up more than $20 billion in annual electric sales in five years, Lou Pai, president of Enron Capital & Trade Resources said.
"That's a fairly conservative number," Pai said, mapping out in detail Enron's targets for competing in the emerging deregulated electric market in North America.

Enron is the largest of several power marketing firms vying for a share of deregulated natural gas and electric industries that generate a combined $305 billion in sales in North America. Once controlled by regulated monopolies, those markets are being opened to competition that has sparked a wave of consolidations among gas and electric companies.

Enron has budgeted $25 million a year in the coming years to build a U.S. electric franchise that will include more than 9,000 employees, about 8 million customers and nearly 100 offices across the country, Pai said in a presentation to the company's bankers.

After completing its acquisition of Oregon electric utility Portland General Corp, Enron expects to rank as the largest U.S. electric company by year-end. The merger is expected to get the approval of state regulators if the two sides can come to an agreement on savings to be passed along to Oregon electric customers, Pai said.

Enron is on track to move 33 million megawatt hours of electricity in the first quarter, continuing exponential growth that left the company with a 29 percent market share of the non-regulated electric wholesale market through the first nine months of last year, Pai said.
